hyperedges.label: CPF test-suite pages and shared cases

nodes.label: Dimension gap (§3.6)
nodes.rationale: CPF.dimensionGap(current, target) returns a state (ok / incertezza_probatoria / nessun_obiettivo) and a numeric gap; probatory uncertainty produces no gap number.

nodes.label: Essential shortfall (§3.6)
nodes.rationale: CPF.essentialShortfall(entry) classifies an essential capability below its non-compensable threshold as divario_essenziale (corroborated) or verifica (level not determinable).

nodes.label: Domain ranking (§3.6)
nodes.rationale: CPF.rankDomains(capability_assessment, criticality) and CPF.domainPriority(entry, criticality) derive per-domain intervention and verification bands, contextualized by function criticality.

nodes.label: Four independent capability dimensions
nodes.rationale: consolidamento, estensione, efficacia, prestazione_osservata — ordinal 1-5, describing a state not a percentage; assessed independently for the current profile.

nodes.label: Function criticality (§3.2)
nodes.rationale: Ordinal 1-4 scale (Bassa/Media/Alta/Molto alta) from CER arts. 6-7, collected in Step 2; feeds the substantive priority in §3.6 f(criticality, essentiality, gap); kept separate from verification priority when evidentiary strength is not corroborated.

nodes.label: Descriptive-only aggregate (§3.7)
nodes.rationale: Scales are ordinal not cardinal; any aggregate is a descriptive indicator only and essential gaps are not absorbed into it. A green outcome means internal coherence of the assessment with the model, not compliance.

nodes.label: Intervention vs verification priority (§3.6)
nodes.rationale: Two distinct outcomes, never merged: priority of intervention (corroborated gaps, essential shortfalls) and priority of verification (uncertain levels, thresholds on non-determinable levels). The ordering is ordinal, not a measure.

nodes.label: Target profile (§3.6)
nodes.rationale: The target level per dimension must be motivated a priori from the consequence to avoid, not adapted to the capabilities already present. Derived (reconcileTargets) from the domains marked required across the compromise paths.

nodes.label: Evidentiary strength separate from level (§3.6)
nodes.rationale: corroborata / parziale / non_determinabile is separate from the level: 'non determinabile' does not lower the level, it suspends the gap and generates a verification priority, not an intervention priority.

nodes.label: CPF measurement model (Ch. 3)
nodes.rationale: Unit of analysis is the cyber-physical function, not the organization or sector; four independent capability dimensions on cumulative 1-5 scales; current/target profile; essential capabilities carry non-compensable thresholds never absorbed into a mean; uncertainty does not lower a level but produces a distinct verification priority.

nodes.label: Dumbbell gap chart (replaces radar)
nodes.rationale: §3.6 allows an aggregate value only as a secondary descriptive/comparative indicator and §3.7 warns the scales are ordinal not cardinal; a filled-area radar communicates false reassurance at a glance. Instead, per domain: one row per dimension with current dot to target ring, gap as a bar, evidentiary strength in the marker style, non-compensable threshold as a vertical line.

nodes.label: Multi-regime classification
nodes.rationale: Item-by-item motivated classification across NIS2, CER, DORA, PSNC, CRA, Regolamento Macchine, AI Act (+ Reg. UE 2026/1744) with an explicit trace; a notified qualification prevails over the orientative calculation.

nodes.label: Regime interactions
nodes.rationale: Interactions between applicable regimes (e.g. DORA lex specialis over NIS2, PSNC national prevalence by scope on Perimeter assets) surfaced from regimeRules.interactions when both members of a pair are relevant.

nodes.label: Size-cap rule (NIS2)
nodes.rationale: Enterprise size (Recommendation 2003/361/EC) brings medium and large enterprises into the NIS2 perimeter.

nodes.label: Regulatory verification priority
nodes.rationale: verification_flags: points where the classification depends on a case-by-case designation or an unconfirmed qualification and needs to be verified rather than assumed.

nodes.label: Client-side persistence (localStorage + JSON import/export)
nodes.rationale: Static client-side app, no server, no build step; assessments and organization profiles live in localStorage and are exportable/importable as JSON, with a quota guard in assets/app.js.

nodes.label: Function-definition coherence heuristics
nodes.rationale: CPF.reviewFunction is heuristic help, not legal validation: flags missing fields, a name that reads like the organization, service description equal to physical process, criticality unmotivated or incoherent with regimes. Findings never block advancing.

nodes.label: Dependency flow diagram (upstream/downstream SVG)
nodes.rationale: Inline-SVG depFlow renders upstream nodes -> function -> downstream nodes, critical links drawn in red; a stand-in until the d3-sankey visualization is added.

nodes.label: B->A dependency notation (§3.4)
nodes.rationale: Every dependency is an oriented relation B -> A: B is the origin (supplier, upstream asset, other element), A is normally the function itself or one of its components.

nodes.label: Critical link (tight coupling + no alternative)
nodes.rationale: A dependency with tight coupling, no available alternative and position not downstream is a critical link: a perturbation propagates without margin. Computed by depCritical / depIssues and highlighted in the editor and dashboard.

nodes.label: Dependency taxonomy: class / coupling / position / failure (§3.4)
nodes.norm_label: dependency taxonomy: class / coupling / position / failure (§3.4)
nodes.rationale: Classes of dependency, tight vs loose coupling, position upstream/internal/downstream with its role in the model, and failure types (common cause E -> {A,B}, cascading A -> B -> C).

nodes.label: Dependency curves / temporal dimension
nodes.rationale: Operational state (normal / stressed / repair-restoration) and tolerable activation time qualify a dependency over time; tight coupling without a quantified margin is flagged.

nodes.label: Reusable organization regime profile
nodes.rationale: Step 1 produces an organization-level regime_profile saved to localStorage; each new function assessment clones it via CPF.cloneRegimeProfile / newAssessmentFromOrg, and the clone stays editable per assessment with an overridden_from_org_profile flag per field.

nodes.label: Per-function regime override (§3.2)
nodes.rationale: The regimes relevant to a function are a subset of the organization profile, but a single function can fall under a regime that does not concern the organization as a whole (e.g. CRA for one digital product); every deviation is flagged overridden_from_org_profile with a reason.

nodes.label: CCE logic (consequence-driven)
nodes.rationale: Consequence-driven, cyber-informed engineering: start from the consequence to avoid, back-trace the compromise paths, identify required capabilities and the essential ones that interrupt them. Generates the target profile and the essential-capability list used in Step 4b.

nodes.label: Intolerable consequences (§3.1)
nodes.rationale: A list of outcomes to exclude (loss of process control, harm to operators/environment, prolonged interruption of an essential service), not a list of threats.

nodes.label: Required vs essential capabilities
nodes.rationale: Per path, the capabilities needed to interrupt it are marked required; those without which the path is not stoppable are marked essential (only enabled when required is set).

nodes.label: Bochman & Freeman, Countering Cyber Sabotage (2021), INL
nodes.norm_label: bochman & freeman, countering cyber sabotage (2021), inl

nodes.label: Non-compensable threshold / weak link (§3.6)
nodes.rationale: For an essential capability, one dimension has a minimum level below which the capability is not adequate and no strength on the other dimensions compensates; it is never absorbed into a mean and forces the intervention priority to high.
